passage: Nursery note, Tuesday. From the doorway I saw Mahima push an arm into the gap behind the sofa, tug at the teddy and fail. Mahima stopped, looked at the gap and walked off to the blocks without a word to anyone. The teddy stayed behind the sofa until I found it much later. At nap time Mahima asked for it and cried when it was not there. I found it and we talked about pointing and saying "stuck." Mehak

qa.q: Where did Mahima walk off to?
qa.a: Mahima walked off to the blocks.

qa.q: What was Mahima feeling at nap time when the teddy was not there?
qa.a: Mahima was sad and missed the teddy, and the crying shows the loss had not been forgotten.

qa.q: What could Mahima try instead of walking away, and why?
qa.a: Mahima could tell Mehak or point at the gap, because an adult can reach the teddy and solve the problem quickly.

qa.q: How does Mehak see the missing teddy?
qa.a: Mehak saw the failed try but was not told, so the teddy was lost until nap time, and Mehak wants Mahima to learn to ask.

grounding: A toddler stops trying to free a wedged teddy, walks away and tells no one, so the toy stays lost until a caregiver finds it later.

passage: Pallavi's cloth teddy slipped behind the heavy cot in the house near the temple tank. She reached into the gap. Stuck. She reached again, then stood, turned and wandered out to the courtyard to play with the goat's kid. She didn't tell anyone. Two days later, sweeping, her grandfather Gautam found the dusty teddy and held it up. "Pallavi! Look who was hiding!"

qa.q: What might Pallavi have been feeling when she wandered out?
qa.a: She was probably frustrated and gave up, turning to the goat's kid to forget the stuck teddy.

qa.q: What else could Pallavi try next time?
qa.a: She could take Gautam's hand and lead him to the cot, so the teddy comes back the same day.

qa.q: How might Gautam feel finding the teddy?
qa.a: He is happy and playful about it, holding it up and calling her.

grounding: A toddler gives up on a wedged teddy, walks away without telling anyone, and the toy stays lost until her grandfather finds it.

passage: Diego pushed his fist behind the sofa in the Valencia flat, but the stuffed dog was wedged too far. He pulled his arm back, looked at the gap, and toddled off to the balcony to watch pigeons. He said nothing to anyone. That night he cried at bedtime without the dog. The next morning his father Gabriel moved the sofa and found it. "There you are!"

qa.a: It was wedged behind the sofa.

qa.q: What was Diego feeling at bedtime?
qa.a: He was sad and upset without his dog, crying at bedtime.

qa.q: What would you advise Diego to try when a toy gets stuck?
qa.a: Go and get Gabriel and point at the gap, so it can be found before bedtime.

qa.q: How might Gabriel see the lost dog?
qa.a: Gabriel probably feels relieved when he finds it, and may wish Diego had told him the day before.

grounding: A toddler stops trying when his toy is wedged, tells no one, and it stays lost until his father finds it later.
